candidates.tagline: CEO calls them 'highly wearable' while frames visibly crush his earlobes
candidates.story: Snap launched its $2,195 Specs AR glasses on September 16, 2026 — glasses that weigh three times more than regular sunglasses — and CEO Evan Spiegel's keynote clip immediately went viral for showing the 'highly wearable' frames pressing visibly into his earlobes while he described them as comfortable; the company has already burned hundreds of millions on unsold earlier-generation Spectacles.
candidates.why_funny: Snap's answer to the 'smart glasses look dorky' problem was to build glasses weighing four times more than normal ones, have the CEO declare them 'highly wearable' in a clip that showed them crushing his ears, and charge $2,195 for the privilege.
candidates.alt: Snap CEO Evan Spiegel on a darkened stage wearing the bulky Snap Specs AR glasses during the September 2026 consumer launch keynote in Los Angeles, with the chunky frames visibly pressing against the sides of his head

candidates.tagline: Apple's $1,999 foldable phone is unusable for left-handers — again
candidates.story: Apple's first foldable iPhone, the Duo, launched September 9 at $1,999, but its Touch ID fingerprint sensor and Camera Control button sit exclusively on the right edge — the same right-biased design that sparked antennagate in 2010 — leaving the 10.6% of users who are left-handed unable to comfortably unlock or shoot photos on a phone Apple markets as its most ambitious ever.
candidates.why_funny: After Steve Jobs' infamous 'you're holding it wrong' response in 2010, Apple spent 16 years and released a $2,000 foldable phone that once again asks left-handed users to hold it differently.
candidates.alt: The Apple iPhone Duo foldable phone shown both folded and open, with the Touch ID fingerprint sensor and Camera Control button visible only on the right side of the device
